races.name: Kenny Developments Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bridge View Star
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map; not raced for 302 days and form reads 6-6-4-6 with no wins or places in similar going, making the fitness angle a significant concern before style is even considered.

runners_data.name: Deeter
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 120, but the fading-in-finish flag and a form line of P-0 in just two hurdle runs are deeply unconvincing; natural rear-runner shuffled into a midfield slot, and trainer McCarthy has two wins from eight over 14 days which is the sole positive angle.

runners_data.name: En Or
runners_data.note: Has winning and placing form on soft and good-to-soft ground (1W3P from 15 sim-going runs) making the conditions genuinely suit; held up naturally but the map places him in midfield, so a clean passage through a 23-runner field is the critical variable.

runners_data.name: Firebrand
runners_data.note: The most consistent profile in the race with five consecutive placings (3-2-2-5-4) at 16-18f on good and soft ground; rides as a genuine prominent-style horse for trainer John Nallen, and the 5lb claimer O'Sullivan adds some positional uncertainty but the form is solid.

runners_data.name: Its Time For A Run
runners_data.note: Won over 19f on good ground last time out and is the form pick among the hold-up contingent; Emmet Mullins yard is going well, but the horse's natural rear-running style is compromised by a field of this size where genuine closers are squeezed.

runners_data.name: Leva Eagle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced, no recent form available, unknown going preference — the UNKNOWN tags mean this runner carries maximum uncertainty and must be treated with caution in any scenario assessment.

runners_data.name: Minnatrix
runners_data.note: Fading-in-finish flag plus a form line of F-S-8-9-2 showing the single placing deep in a smaller field; five runs on good ground without winning suggests a ceiling rather than an upward curve.

runners_data.name: Morale Boost
runners_data.note: Unknown style, lightly raced, and returning after 121 days off under trainer Gary McGill who is winless over 14 days; form reads 1-2-5-P suggesting some ability but the confidence case is very thin.

runners_data.name: Mr Caulfield
runners_data.note: A placed run at 21f on good ground is the most relevant piece of form; ridden by a 7lb claimer and returning just seven days after his last run, with trainer Noel Kelly showing no wins from 14 runners over 14 days — modest profile.

runners_data.name: Papanell
runners_data.note: Placed once at 16f on good ground from four starts; consistent without threatening, trainer John Joseph Murphy has no wins in the 14-day window, and the form ceiling appears modest.

runners_data.name: Piper Street
runners_data.note: Only one run on record (6th at 16f on good ground) giving very little to work with; P J Rothwell has two wins from 25 runners over 14 days, and the unknown quantity here is almost entirely a negative in a field this competitive.

runners_data.name: Tribal Thunder
runners_data.note: Tagged UNKNOWN style and lightly raced; returning from 120 days off, form includes a 9th last time, and jockey J J Slevin's class is the one interesting angle — but the horse needs to show more than it has so far.

runners_data.name: Blue Nude
runners_data.note: Four runs, four finishes of 8-8-11-16 with a persistent fading flag; despite being placed in midfield, this is a natural hold-up horse and the record on good ground is uniformly poor — the redistribution simply reinforces a weak profile.

runners_data.name: Getaway Tobin
runners_data.note: Won 4th and 5th in two of four good-ground starts but no wins; tongue-tie worn and a natural hold-up horse bumped into a midfield berth — trainer McConnell has a healthy 4/29 strike rate over 14 days which is the one live angle.

runners_data.name: Hometomayo
runners_data.note: A persistent fader who has finished 9th, pulled up, or mid-field in all three hurdle runs; returning after 48 days for trainer Flannery who has no 14-day winners, and the true hold-up style further reduces any practical chance in a steady-pace race.

runners_data.name: Leva Deva
runners_data.note: Four runs on good ground, best finish a 9th, and the fading-in-finish flag combined with a natural hold-up style squeezed into midfield makes this a difficult race for the horse regardless of scenario — 14 days since last run is recent enough but form gives nothing to build on.

runners_data.name: Middlethird Marvel
runners_data.note: Six runs on good ground without a win or a place — form reads 0-6-0-P-13-11 — and the fade flag plus natural hold-up style mapped to midfield makes this one of the weakest risk-reward profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Rene's Gold
runners_data.note: Two hurdle runs (9th and 8th on good ground) both featuring a finishing fade; trainer O'Sullivan has one win from 18 in the 14-day window, but the form and finishing pattern point firmly toward a horse who is not yet finding a way to the front.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Everyday
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race, handled by Townend for Mullins, and crucially has placed form at 16-17f on soft and good ground (1W2P from 7 sim-going runs) — controls the pace entirely and the race revolves around whether she can hold on.

runners_data.name: Minella Maverick
runners_data.note: No jockey declared, no recent form available, lightly raced — the blank profile means this runner is as close to unassessable as any in the field.

runners_data.name: Stary Notions
runners_data.note: No jockey declared, no form record, returning from an unspecified layoff for a trainer with no 14-day winners — zero evidence to support confidence in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Misty Valentine
runners_data.note: Three runs all ending in unseating, pulling up or 15th place; the fading flag and a form line of P-0-U on good ground makes this a non-factor for scenario purposes, with safety on course the more pressing consideration.

races.paceDynamic: Wonderful Everyday (Paul Townend/W P Mullins) is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-horse field and should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on yielding ground without any genuine rival looking to burn her off. With Townend aboard, she is almost certain to be allowed to stride along at her own tempo, making this a relatively sedate pace scenario for a maiden hurdle of this size, which strongly rewards horses who can travel close to the pace and strike off a steady gallop rather than closers who need a genuine test of stamina. The field holds materially more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Middlethird Marvel, Leva Deva, Its Time For A Run, Blue Nude, Getaway Tobin, Hometomayo and Deeter are all natural hold-up horses who are effectively mapped to midfield and are unlikely to find their true position, meaning the back of the field will be congested and finishers will face traffic problems. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can track Wonderful Everyday from second or third position, travel comfortably and quicken from the front of the chasing pack, hold a decisive positional advantage in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wonderful Everyday Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Everyday is allowed to bowl along at her own pace with no rival applying pressure, Townend controls the race from the front and the chasing group never gets close enough to threaten.
scenarios.body: Wonderful Everyday sets an unhurried, rhythm-friendly gallop on yielding Galway ground, and the sheer size of the field means traffic problems eliminate many hold-up types before the final flight; she makes all and holds on from those racing close in her slipstream.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Everyday's pace is steady enough to keep a nearby prominent type fresh, a horse tracking in second or third sweeps past from the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Firebrand has the profile here — consistent form figures of 2-2-3-4-5 in similar good-ground conditions, Galway experience, and a style that allows racing just off the pace; a prominent runner with clean jumping and a clear run could cut down Wonderful Everyday on the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Cause Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften up the leaders and create a truly run race, a hold-up horse picks through late traffic to nail a tiring front group.
scenarios.body: This shape requires a faster early gallop than Wonderful Everyday typically sets and depends on redistributed hold-up types actually finding clear daylight through a 23-runner field — both conditions are difficult to satisfy simultaneously; Its Time For A Run, the only hold-up horse here with a recent win on good ground, is best placed if gaps materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If the large field produces significant jumping errors, falls or interference at key hurdles, the race is effectively run as a survival test and the result hinges on fortune rather than ability.
scenarios.body: In a 23-runner Galway maiden on yielding ground, fallers or loose horses reshaping the flow cannot be discounted; Wonderful Everyday, being alone at the front, may actually be insulated from this while midfield horses are most vulnerable to being impeded or brought down.

watchPoints.text: Wonderful Everyday (Townend/Mullins) controls the entire pace map as the sole front-runner — if she gets a clean round and dictates a comfortable gallop, the race is effectively hers to lose and all other scenarios weaken proportionally.

The 23-runner field on a yielding Galway track creates serious traffic risk from the third-last hurdle home — hold-up horses En Or, Its Time For A Run and Mr Caulfield are the most likely to be blocked at a crucial moment despite having the ability to threaten.

Firebrand's consistency (five consecutive placings, never worse than 5th in recent starts) is real, but the 5lb claim on O'Sullivan in a big field on yielding ground adds a positional management uncertainty that could cost the horse its natural rhythm.

Trainer P J Rothwell saddles three runners (Piper Street, Blue Nude, You Lift Me Up) with a 2/25 recent strike rate — monitor for any market moves suggesting stable confidence, as the stable runner count gives them multiple tactical options even if none stands out on form.

Leva Eagle and Minella Maverick carry no form, no jockey declarations and unknown styles — watch the betting market for late support on either, as unexposed horses from unknown stables occasionally arrive at Galway with hidden ability that the data cannot surface.

races.name: Anglo Printers Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beckistine
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator 230 days off the track for M A Molloy; similar-going record shows one placed effort from six, and the lengthy absence combined with a big field makes finding clear air a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning from a 230-day absence, Beckistine faces a stiff ask here — that pulled-up effort latest is a concern, though he has run over today's trip and carries a manageable weight at 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Mart Lane
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Barry Connell who arrives on a short turnaround (42 days); all five recent runs have been over 16f on soft or good-to-soft and he handles the going without issue, though he has yet to win at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Mart Lane arrives here 42 days fresh and showed a second three starts back, yet he has been winless in his last five outings and an eighth last time out raises questions about current form; he has run over today's trip and our rating of 106 gives him a shout, but 164 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Palace Boy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse fitted with a blindfold; only one win from 14 runs on similar ground and the amateur jockey claiming 7lb faces a stern test in a 23-runner contest.
runners_data.comment: Palace Boy has run over today's trip and going, and with our rating of 110 putting him third among 23 rivals, he clearly holds strong claims — the risk is that he remains winless in his last four starts, with only a fifth the best he could manage recently.

runners_data.name: Inthenickoftime
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer for E Bolger who won over 18f on good ground last time; 2W8P from 15 similar-going runs is an outstanding strike rate and the 35-day break looks ideal — one of the few horses whose natural style fits this race shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well for a third last time out, and a winner five starts back, but a pulled-up effort three starts back and a career-high 163 lb are the main negatives; he does have experience over today's trip and going, and returns after a 35-day break in reasonable nick.

runners_data.name: Crowsatedappletart
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-to-lead type with four wins from 15 similar-going starts; fitted with a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, has won over both 16f and 19f on soft ground and Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim is a bonus at the weights.
runners_data.comment: Crowsatedappletart won two starts back and our rating of 112 marks him out as a serious player here; he has experience over today's trip and conditions, and 35 days between runs leaves him fresh. The sixth last time out is the one worry.

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a tongue-strap who stays well (3rd over 24f on good recently); only 17 days since last run and Philip Byrnes takes the mount, but his hold-up style in a 23-runner field makes finding space a lottery.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Paul Collins does at least return on a reasonable 17-day break with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; a third three starts back offers some encouragement, though 162 lb and a mixed recent record are obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: I'm All In
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott four-year-old who carries a fades-in-finish flag; just two runs on yielding-comparable ground with no placed efforts, and the pattern of fading makes him unreliable if the pace drops late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, I'm All In faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and returns after 25 days, but a string of eighths, ninths, and two unseated-rider incidents make him very hard to fancy at 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Jay Jay Zee
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Charlie Keegan returning after 144 days off; 1W3P from eight similar-going runs is a decent profile and the longer trip (22f form on record) suggests stamina is not an issue, though the layoff is a question mark.
runners_data.comment: Jay Jay Zee has run over today's trip and going, carries a hefty 160 lb yet our rating of 110 marks him out as a live threat in a 23-runner field; winless in recent starts and that fall on his latest outing is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted hold-up type who ran just 12 days ago; all seven recent runs on good ground show no wins, and while the quick turnaround suggests fitness, he finds this field considerably deeper than anything he has faced.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Codger's Rock does at least bring distance experience and a fitness edge at just 12 days since his latest run, though a top weight of 158 lb looks a stiff ask for a gelding whose recent form reads 6th, unplaced, and 6th.

runners_data.name: Roc My Haarth
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-held-up performer who won over 23f on soft on his most recent start 158 days ago; the long absence is the key risk, but the stamina profile and soft-ground form are genuine assets if the race develops into a test of staying power.
runners_data.comment: Roc My Haarth won last time out but returns after a 158-day absence carrying 154 lb, and while he has run over today's going before, his inconsistent recent form — including an unseated — means fitness and temperament are both questions here.

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear is oversubscribed in this field; STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects that he is unlikely to get his natural berth, and six wins/places from 15 good-ground runs has not included a win — discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15 of 23 on our ratings, Synchronize faces a stiff ask under 154 lb, though he has run over today's trip before and 23 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Dontcavein
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and the pivotal horse in the race shape; 209 days off the track for Ciaran Murphy and no similar-going form in the last five runs, but his role as unchallenged pace-setter is confirmed and the tongue-tie is retained.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Dontcavein arrives 209 days later carrying 153 lb, which is no small ask; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 103 offers some encouragement, but the layoff and recent decline make him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Euro Maker
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on good ground but carries a fades-in-finish flag and is a true hold-up horse forced into a midfield role by the weight of hold-up runners; STYLE_FIT 0.92 and the finishing pattern make him hard to fancy in a scenario where he cannot get his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Euro Maker returns after 28 days and has run over today's trip and going, but ranked 18 of 23 on our figures he faces a stiff ask, and a pulled-up effort lurking in recent starts does little to inspire confidence despite that latest win.

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton runner who has failed to complete on occasions and fades in finishes; genuinely a hold-up horse but will not be sitting last in this 23-runner field, reducing his chance further — STYLE_FIT 0.90 reflects he will be racing out of role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a sixth, two further disappointing efforts and an unseating rider in that sequence, Kome Dans Un Reve is hard to fancy on these figures, though he has run over today's trip before and 25 days off may have freshened him up.

runners_data.name: Brother Hollie
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Mark Michael McNiff, last seen finishing third over 18f on good 57 days ago; genuine hold-up style but the redistribution to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.93) means he will not get his favoured position — the form profile is modest and the field competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 57 days off, Brother Hollie does have experience over today's trip and that encouraging third last time out offers a glimmer, though a rating of 96 and 151 lb on his back make progress far from straightforward.

runners_data.name: Colin's Friend
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old returning after 216 days, ridden by the high-profile Darragh O'Keeffe; trainer has a strong 14-day strike rate (5/25) but the lengthy layoff and true hold-up style in a packed field reduce his winning prospects significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after 216 days off the track, Colin's Friend has questions to answer on fitness, though he has experience over today's trip and conditions and a career-high weight of 151 lb is another test.

runners_data.name: Hillstar Blues
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes and is a true hold-up horse displaced into midfield by the sheer number of similar types; amateur rider Anna McGuinness (7lb claim) adds an additional layer of risk and the record in similar going is unremarkable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Hillstar Blues carries a hefty 151 lb and is yet to translate his 99 rating into results, though he has run over today's trip and 24 days between runs suggests he returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Arctic Piper
runners_data.note: Returning 25 days after last run with a record of pulled-up and fell efforts in recent starts; genuine hold-up type who will be caught between roles in this field, and the inconsistent jumping profile is a concern in a big hurdles field.
runners_data.comment: Arctic Piper has pulled up twice and fallen in her last five starts, making her extremely difficult to fancy, and winless throughout that spell; the one plus is she has run over today's distance and going before, and 25 days off gives her a fair enough preparation.

runners_data.name: I Feel Fine
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for M A Molloy (same yard as Beckistine) who fades in finishes; six runs on similar ground without a win and the redistribution to midfield means he will race out of his preferred position — no strong angle here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 21 of 23 on our figures, I Feel Fine is hard to fancy, having pulled up and unseated in recent outings; he has run over today's trip before, and 53 days between runs at least suggests connections are patient.

runners_data.name: Million Dollar Man
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old with a disappointing recent record (P-600) and a fades-in-finish flag; just three similar-going runs available and STYLE_FIT 0.90 confirms he will be out of role in the race's actual shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up on his most recent completed effort, Million Dollar Man heads into this carrying 149 lb off a 65-day absence, with his trainer in poor nick at 1/36 recently — though a rating of 97 suggests some latent ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: Speakasyoufind
runners_data.note: No jockey listed, which is worth monitoring at declaration stage; fades in finishes and STYLE_FIT 0.91 reflects he is a true hold-up horse unlikely to get his natural position — second over 20f on good ground is the best form on offer but the finishing pattern is worrying.
runners_data.comment: Speakasyoufind has experience over today's trip but is winless in his last five starts and ranks 19th of 23 on our figures, making him hard to fancy; a fall last time and a pulled-up effort in the mix only add to the concern, though a second three starts back offers a sliver of hope.

runners_data.name: Black Bamboo
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 114 in this field, a nine-year-old hold-up performer who has not placed in five recent runs on similar ground; the burden of 174lbs and a poor recent profile make it difficult to construct a winning scenario even if the race developed into a stamina test.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle's five-year-old who has been running consistently in modest company, all recent form on good ground at 16-17f; true hold-up type redistributed into midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.91) and the form profile does not suggest she is competitive off OR 80 in this grade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 20th of 23 on our figures, Cinnabar Moth is hard to fancy despite carrying 140 lb with experience over today's trip and going; a fourth last time out is her best recent showing.

races.paceDynamic: Dontcavein is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, critically, faces no meaningful pace pressure from any other genuine lead horse, meaning he can bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo on yielding ground without ever being harried. Inthenickoftime and Crowsatedappletart are the most likely to press him from a prominent position, and with Roc My Haarth also capable of racing handy, the early order will be compact but not chaotic. From there, the field's many hold-up types — the majority of the field by style count — will be forced to race further forward than ideal simply because the rear is congested, and a steady gallop set by a lone front-runner does nothing to help them generate a winning run late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up-to-prominent horses who can travel in the first four or five and pounce from a close position, with the sustainable pace and yielding ground rewarding those who conserve energy near the front rather than those making ground from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dontcavein Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dontcavein is allowed to dictate a truly uncontested and honest-but-not-suicidal gallop and none of the prominent horses are able to close the gap at the business end.
scenarios.body: Dontcavein travels comfortably in front on yielding ground with no rival willing or able to apply sustained pressure, reaching the final two hurdles with a clear rhythm advantage; horses close enough to challenge at the second-last are best placed, meaning prominent racers Inthenickoftime and Crowsatedappletart — who have the form to sit just behind the leader — are the chief beneficiaries if they can pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Inthenickoftime or Crowsatedappletart moves smoothly into contention from the second-last and the leader begins to empty in the final 150 yards.
scenarios.body: Both horses have proven form at similar trips and going, and Crowsatedappletart in particular has a strong record on soft-to-good ground and has won at this sort of trip before; Inthenickoftime won over 18f on good recently and is operating off a manageable mark, making this a prime setup for a held-up-to-prominent winner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to create a stamina test in the closing stages and a big-field cavalry charge develops from the rear.
scenarios.body: This is a harder task than it looks — many horses mapped at the rear are redistributed true hold-up types who will not actually be sitting last, reducing the pool of authentic closers; Mart Lane or Jay Jay Zee, with solid form at this trip and going, are the most plausible beneficiaries if they find a clear run in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Big-Field Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Dontcavein sets a pace that is too extreme for the conditions and collapses approaching the last, triggering a scramble from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A 23-runner field on yielding ground always carries some risk of positional carnage and fallers disrupting the shape, but Dontcavein's modest OR of 93 and lack of experience at this trip make a pace collapse at least plausible; in that scenario, horses who had tracked in the first six or seven lengths would benefit, with Roc My Haarth — last seen winning over 23f on soft — best placed to capitalise on stamina grounds.

watchPoints.text: Dontcavein sets the entire race tempo unchallenged — if he gets 200m of daylight in a 23-runner yielding-ground field, he could prove very hard to peg back and any horse caught flat-footed early is effectively out of the race.

The 23-runner field on yielding ground dramatically increases the risk of scrimmaging at the first hurdle and positional interference through the early stages — horses drawn wide or slow away may lose ten lengths before the race settles.

Inthenickoftime and Crowsatedappletart both want to race prominently and there is a genuine risk they compete with each other for the same prominent position, potentially forcing one into a pace it does not want to sustain.

Multiple hold-up horses carrying STYLE_FIT flags of 0.90–0.93 — including Synchronize, Euro Maker, Brother Hollie and Kome Dans Un Reve — will be racing out of their natural role; watch to see if any of them manage to get further back than expected and whether that produces a late run or simply leaves them with too much ground to make up.

races.name: Deacy Gilligan Hurdle

runners_data.name: Thecompanysergeant
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up stayer with 1W5P on similar going and a course win over 20f on good; Conor Stone-Walsh takes over for Cromwell (1/36 last 14 days), and the 9yo's stamina at this trip on yielding is a serious asset if held up and produced late.
runners_data.comment: Thecompanysergeant arrives here on the back of a win three starts back and brings experience of today's distance and going, returning after 24 days in good heart; the concern is a trainer firing at just 3% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: Mullins/Townend combination with a 2W8P similar-going record and the clear lead role — this 7yo has won at 18f on good and placed at 20f on soft, and with no one to press him, the question is purely whether he's done enough in 36 days off to last home over an extra half-mile.
runners_data.comment: Blood Destiny arrives in fine fettle, a winner last time out and second two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going to call on; the 154 lb burden is the one query, but his profile makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Buddy One
runners_data.note: Gilligan rides for his own trainer in what looks a sentimental entry, but the 9yo's 1W3P on similar going and fourth at 20f on heavy suggest he stays well; recent form (6P40-8) is modest and the 40-day break is a concern, though the hg:p (hood) can help sharpen him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Buddy One nonetheless steps up fit enough after 40 days and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while carrying 154 lb with an official rating of 142 — the chief concern being that his recent form, including a pull-up, makes it hard to trust him fully.

runners_data.name: French Dynamite
runners_data.note: 11yo returning from 279 days off is the single biggest flag here — he has a strong 2W6P similar-going record and has proven himself over 24f on soft, but a near-nine-month absence for McNamara's yard (0/3 last 14 days) makes it hard to trust him fully first time back.
runners_data.comment: French Dynamite brings strong recent form to the table — a winner two starts back, with a runner-up finish last time out — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while our rating of 148 marks him out as a leading contender; the concern is a 279-day absence.

runners_data.name: Grann's Boy
runners_data.note: Won last time at 22f on good and holds 4W5P on similar going — the 6yo is lightly raced and likely still improving, and Flanagan from prominent will ensure he travels close enough to the pace to exploit any weakness from Blood Destiny in the final climb.
runners_data.comment: Grann's Boy won last time out but that victory sits alongside an unplaced effort and a ninth in recent starts, leaving his consistency open to question; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 37 days since that win leaves fitness a minor query under 154 lb.

runners_data.name: Milan Forth
runners_data.note: Cavanagh's 7yo is a genuine prominent racer by nature but finds himself pressed further back than ideal in this field — his 3W5P on similar going is solid, yet a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 signals he will not get the close-up position that suits him and his chance is meaningfully discounted as a result.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Milan Forth looks up against it here, though a third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer faint encouragement; 41 days off means fitness must also be taken on trust.

runners_data.name: Samui
runners_data.note: Elliott's 7yo (2/35 last 14 days, 10 days since last run) is a natural hold-up horse placed repeatedly on similar going (15/15 compatible), but he too finds the map tighter than ideal and his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 reflects that he races out of his preferred position; the tp headgear suggests Elliott is trying to engage him, and recent form (2nd last time) is solid.

races.paceDynamic: Blood Destiny (Paul Townend, Mullins) is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m5½f on yielding ground. The prominent brigade — French Dynamite, Grann's Boy, and Paul's Dream — will likely settle just off the pace, creating a compact, organised early shape rather than a pressured one. This field contains more prominent-leaning types than can all occupy that territory: Blood Destiny is almost certain to secure the lead, with Grann's Boy and French Dynamite most likely to lock in the prominent slots ahead of the redistributed Milan Forth, who will be shuffled further back than his natural style. A lone, uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace over a staying trip on soft-ish ground strongly favours the hold-up and staying-prominent profiles who can travel within themselves and deliver a sustained finish — closers with stamina and form on this type of ground are best placed to exploit the steady early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blood Destiny Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop and Townend times his race to perfection, never getting headed.
scenarios.body: Blood Destiny's lone front-running role means he controls every aspect of the tempo, and on yielding ground at a distance he handles (1W over 20f on soft), he could simply never be caught if the pace is misjudged by those in behind. Townend's ability to conserve energy from the front and quicken marginally at the last is the critical factor, and his record on this type at Galway is formidable.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stayers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny's advantage is eroded in the final mile as the true stayers in behind travel more comfortably through a steady pace.
scenarios.body: Thecompanysergeant and Buddy One, genuine hold-up operators with stamina (both proven over 22f+) and strong similar-going records, will be produced to challenge from off the pace as the race develops, with Blood Destiny vulnerable if he has used himself up controlling a potentially slow early gallop. Thecompanysergeant's 1W5P on similar going and win over this course type makes him the most dangerous closer if the pace falls away in the home straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and French Dynamite or Grann's Boy produce their best from a close-up position to outstay the field.
scenarios.body: French Dynamite (2W6P on similar going, proven over 24f) and Grann's Boy (4W5P on similar going, won last time) are both proven over today's trip and ground and will sit close enough to Blood Destiny to pounce if he flags before the last. Grann's Boy's recent winning form and youth (6yo) give him the stronger profile if this scenario unfolds, with French Dynamite a secondary threat despite 279 days off.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsiders Cause Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically — pace collapses or several horses make errors — leaving Milan Forth or Paul's Dream to take advantage.
scenarios.body: Paul's Dream has shown consecutive wins at smaller tracks and 4W9P on similar going, and could benefit from a muddled race if the leaders tire; however Milan Forth is racing out of his natural prominent role and faces an uphill task shipping back through the field from further than ideal. This is the least likely shape given Blood Destiny's dominance and Townend's tactical awareness.

watchPoints.text: Blood Destiny jumps and travels smoothly — if Townend is foot-perfect at the obstacles and builds a clear lead by halfway, the race could be over as a contest before the home straight.

French Dynamite's 279-day layoff is the single biggest risk factor in the market — watch his paddock demeanour and early miles carefully, as a well-backed returning horse who runs flat could distort the pace picture for those following him.

Milan Forth and Samui are both racing further back than they would naturally choose — if neither can work forward early, their finishing kicks may not materialise as projected and the market may overrate their chances.

Grann's Boy's jockey Sean Flanagan has strong prominent-race judgement and if he slots in second or third behind Blood Destiny from the outset, the 6yo's improving profile and recent win make him a natural race-shape beneficiary to monitor through the final mile.

Going is reported as Yielding for this race despite the official card description of Good to Soft — the distinction matters for stamina horses like Thecompanysergeant and French Dynamite, both of whom have strong profiles on the softer end of the spectrum.

races.paceDynamic: Clone Cross is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 23 and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front over this stiff 2m6½f trip on yielding ground at Galway. With no genuine rival willing or able to seriously press for the lead, the pace is unlikely to be searingly hot, meaning those racing prominently or just off the pace in tracking positions will be ideally placed to conserve energy and pounce. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Coup d'Essay, Princess Felicia, Tedworth, Katie's Casper, Moonshine Girl, Ranger Billy and others have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all get their natural rear positions in a 23-runner race, and several will end up racing further forward than ideal. With pace modest and the trip long enough to stretch stamina, the race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Clone Cross through the final mile and produce a sustained challenge from two out — genuine hold-up horses will need luck in running and a well-judged ride to get competitive from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If Clone Cross sets a steady uncontested gallop and the prominent trackers travel comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Clone Cross dictates a modest tempo over the long Galway trip and those tracking just off the pace expend minimal energy, arriving at the final two hurdles full of running; Joshua Chamberlain and Ladiam, both proven prominent racers at this trip on good ground, are ideally profiled to sustain their challenge to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sustainable and Clone Cross settles well enough to conserve stamina over 2m6½f on yielding ground.
scenarios.body: Clone Cross, racing prominently as confirmed, controls the race throughout and the lack of any serious challenger to the lead means it never has to burn petrol chasing rivals; with a 5yo still improving and good course form on similar going, it becomes very hard to peg back once it quickens at the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected — perhaps through midfield scrimmaging in a 23-runner field — and the race develops a searching gallop that suits closers.
scenarios.body: A competitive 23-runner field creates significant traffic and a more genuine test of stamina, and a horse that threads through from behind late could catch a tiring front rank; Kilkee Bay, a genuine recent winner at course and distance, and John Storey, a consistent stayer in long-trip handicap hurdles, are the most plausible beneficiaries if the race is truly run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scenario — Packed Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant interference, fallers or traffic issues that disrupt the race's rhythm entirely.
scenarios.body: With 23 runners over hurdles on a yielding surface, the risk of a chaotic race with bunching, falls and cut-backs through the field is real; horses drawn or racing wide with cleaner passage — such as Phildante or Moonshine Girl — could benefit from staying out of trouble more than through any tactical superiority.

watchPoints.text: With 23 runners in a 23-runner field at Galway over hurdles on yielding ground, the risk of a mass pile-up or series of fallers at an early hurdle is significant — any horse drawn or tracking wide early (such as Phildante or Kilkee Bay) avoids the worst of the carnage.

Clone Cross has the race entirely on its own terms from the front with no confirmed pace rival — if Kevin Healy goes too steady, the entire field will be in a bunch turning for home and a cavalry charge finish suits no one cleanly, watch for the jockey's tempo judgement in the first mile.

The volume of redistributed hold-up types now racing in midfield — including Coup d'Essay, Princess Felicia, Tedworth and Moonshine Girl — means the middle section of the field will be deeply congested; any horse caught in a pocket turning for home faces a severe passage problem.

The sustainable, uncontested pace this creates means the race will not truly test stamina through compression of the middle stages, instead playing out as a procession until the field meets the rising ground in the Galway straight where the race will quicken sharply late. Grace Faraday, The Vegas Raider, Poetic Focus, and numerous others are genuine hold-up horses who cannot all settle in their natural positions given the size of the field — those most likely to push forward and secure prominent berths are the lower-weighted, handy types such as Strong Contender and Gortmore Lady, who have the tactical versatility to travel closer than their assigned position suggests. The race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can track the pace in a prominent or handy midfield position and produce a sustained late run, with true deep closers at a structural disadvantage given the modest, uncontested tempo Three By Two will set.

scenarios.body: The bunch effect off a slow pace means several midfield horses simultaneously challenge from the three-out position, and those with the best finishing kick on yielding ground prevail in a tight finish; horses with strong form on good-to-yielding who have been freshened up and are suited to the trip hold the edge.

races.paceDynamic: Mongibello is the confirmed front-runner here and, returning from 501 days off, will set out to dictate from the front at a sustainable clip over Galway's 2m2f chase course on yielding ground. This shape — a controlled lead, moderate tempo, and a compressed field into the straight — most strongly favours horses who travel prominently or can race close to the pace and pick up when asked, rewarding clean jumping and tactical efficiency over raw finishing kick. The field holds more genuine prominent-running types than can all secure their natural position; Polepatrick, Ndaawi, and Captain Ryan Matt are all true prominent racers but at least one or two will be forced to race further back than they would ideally prefer, with Ocastle Des Mottes and William Tell best placed to occupy the ground just behind Mongibello.

With yielding ground confirmed throughout the card at Galway, the 2m6½f trip rewards stamina and jumping accuracy over raw speed, so a controlled, single-paced front from Brandt sets up a race that will be largely strung out from halfway with rivals grinding rather than quickening. The bulk of this field — Tell Us This, Granville Street, Juke Hill, Justatan, Oneforgonzo, That's About Right, Nolans Rocco, and Smallcraftwarning — are all genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield simply because the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear; in reality, several will track further back than shown and only one or two will secure a prominent berth. A sustainable, uncontested lead in soft-ish ground over a staying trip strongly favours horses with proven stamina, clean jumping, and the ability to deliver a long, grinding finish — true stayers tracking just off the pace who can reel in a tiring front-runner, rather than hold-up horses dependent on a sprint finish that this shape will not provide.

runners_data.comment: Unraced and completely unexposed, Summer Sandals steps into the unknown on debut carrying 165 lb, but with no form to weigh up she remains an open proposition with improvement entirely possible.

runners_data.name: What'shername
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, What'shername has had a troubled time of late — unseating last time out and again three starts back, with a fall five starts back adding to her woes — but she remains lightly raced enough to be of interest off a long 113-day absence, carrying 165 lb.

runners_data.name: Elusive Moon
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Elusive Moon arrives with her cards firmly to her chest, and at 163 lb she faces a stern early test of mettle — yet to score, but with nothing in the book to count against her either.

runners_data.name: Lake Pippaway
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Lake Pippaway has shown little in her last three starts — including an unseating and a pulled up — but, lightly raced and returning after 100 days, there may be more to come under her 163 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Melody D'Arc
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Melody D'Arc arrives as a complete unknown, yet that cuts both ways — nothing to go on either way first time out, and at 163 lb she steps straight into the spotlight with improvement very much on the cards.

runners_data.name: Mozart's Song
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Mozart's Song carries 163 lb into her first start and remains an unknown quantity, open to significant improvement as connections get their first look at her on a racecourse.

runners_data.name: Prometteuse
runners_data.comment: Prometteuse makes her debut here carrying 163 lb, wholly unexposed and with everything still to learn — but that very openness leaves the door wide ajar, and she merits close watching as her profile takes shape.
